chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding the wealth of the orphan, is there Zakat upon it? He said: When it is a deposit, there is no Zakat upon it, and when you work with it, you are responsible (guarantor) for it, and the profit is for the orphan.
ai.seo_question: Is Zakat due on an orphan's wealth if it is kept as a deposit versus being invested?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a critical distinction in Shia jurisprudence between passive custody and active management of an orphan's wealth. It clarifies that Zakat liability is tied to the wealth's productive status, while the guardian assumes full liability (daman) for the principal if they engage in trade, ensuring that all commercial gains accrue exclusively to the orphan.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the wealth of the orphans, ‘Is there Zakāt upon it?’ So heasws said: ‘When it is a deposit, so there is no Zakāt upon it, but when it is worked with, so you would be responsible (guarantor) for it, and the profit would be for the orphan’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from al-Halabiy who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the assets of the orphans if there is Zakat on it. He (the Imam) said, ‘If it (asset) is not active (not used in business) Zakat is not due on it. If you use it in business, then you are responsible for it and its profit belongs to the orphan.’”
